name: manual_17b561
claim: In a shared local working tree with another live agent, that agent's own periodic/automatic commit sweep can capture and commit YOUR in-progress uncommitted edits under ITS commit message -- verify the actual committed diff is byte-identical to what you intended before assuming it's a collision to fix, rather than redoing the work

decisions.notes: Mid-edit on orchestrator/cost_guard.py (writing reserve/commit/rollback), a commit appeared (cf737081) under the shared 'cyre' git identity with a message I never wrote, at a moment I hadn't run git commit myself. git show confirmed the diff was byte-for-byte identical to my own Edit-tool changes still sitting on disk -- Agnes's own 'commit everything in logical batches' habit had swept up my uncommitted file. Verified via git status (clean, matching disk) and re-ran the full test suite against the committed content before treating it as done, rather than either blindly trusting it or re-doing the work from scratch. Lesson: in this kind of shared-tree multi-agent session, commit your own work promptly and in smaller increments to reduce the window another agent's sweep can grab it out of sequence -- and when you find an unexpected commit, diff it against your own intended changes before reacting, since 'unexpected' doesn't always mean 'wrong.'
